deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 6-8). Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 'tame' (modérée) geometry. A 'modèle' M_* is a system of families M_n (more generally M_I for finite sets I) of subsets of R^n (or R^I), subject to axioms (M0)...(M5). It yields a category Esp_M of M-tame spaces. Each such space has an underlying-set functor X -> |X| and admits transport of structure along bijections (p. 6). Page 6 proves that Esp_M has finite products, indeed finite limits, and that X -> |X| commutes with them. It then introduces axiom (M5): R in M_1, which implies R^I in M_I for every finite I.

This page.
(1) Under (M5), R carries a canonical tame structure, viewing R as a 'modèle' inside R^1 = R. So R is an object of E = Esp_mod.
(2) Every object of E is isomorphic to a subobject of some R^n, the product being taken in E. Every tame space is thus 'affine' or 'embeddable', the analogue of the fact that definable sets live in some R^n.
(3) One recovers M_n as the set of subobjects of R^n in E. The reading 'On récupère' is likely, rather than 'On s'imagine'.
(4) Claimed theorem: giving M_* is equivalent, up to isomorphism, to giving a triple (E, R, |.|):
(a) E is a category with finite projective limits;
(b) |.|: E -> Sets is left exact;
(c) R is an object of E such that every object of E embeds into some R^n.
In modern terms, a 'structure' in the o-minimal or model-theoretic sense, viewed as the system of its definable sets, is recaptured from its category of definable sets. That category comes with a forgetful 'fibre functor' to Sets and a generating object R whose finite powers receive embeddings of all objects. This is a reconstruction statement of Tannakian or categorical-logic flavour, used here to move freely between the 'subset' and 'categorical' descriptions.
(5) Planned items: talk about tame maps of tame spaces into the R^I and introduce cartesian products. A left-margin note says to introduce tame functions as the morphisms of Esp_mod and to establish the properties of the images f(A) and inverse images f^{-1}(B) of tame parts.
(6) Section III opens: 'Limites inductives', i.e. gluings ('jonctions'/recollements) of tame spaces. The question is which colimits exist, built from tame parts, and whether they are preserved by |.|. The continuation on p. 8 treats finite unions, the existence of a unique tame structure on a finite union with tame (discrete) stratifications, pushouts X1 ⊔_Z X2, and a criterion: if the set-theoretic colimit carries a tame structure making the canonical maps tame, it is the colimit in Esp. This matches the later theory of 'definable spaces' obtained by gluing.
errors: The equivalence M_* <-> (E, R, |.|) as stated is incomplete. Condition (b) must also require that |.| is faithful and induces an injection from subobjects of R^n to subsets of |R|^n, i.e. it is mono-preserving and 'conservative on subobjects'. Otherwise M_n = Sub(R^n) is not a family of subsets of R^n, and E is not recovered as a category of sets-with-structure.

If the axioms (M*) include stability under projections/images, as an o-minimal-type theory needs, finite limits alone do not suffice. E would also need image factorizations (regularity) preserved by |.|, and the margin note on f(A) points exactly to this. The page does not state such a condition.
Condition (c) as transcribed reads 'tout objet de R'; it must be 'tout objet de E'.

ideas.what: Under the axiom R in M_1, R becomes a tame space and every tame space embeds into some R^n
ideas.modern_name: Definable sets / affine definable spaces of an o-minimal structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (1984-86); van den Dries, 'Tame topology and o-minimal structures' (1998)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches 'topologie modérée' but not this formalism

ideas.what: Equivalence between a tame 'modèle' M_* and the triple (finitely complete category E, left exact functor |.| to Sets, generating object R with every object embedding in some R^n); M_n recovered as Sub_E(R^n)
ideas.modern_name: Category of definable sets with its forgetful functor, as in categorical logic (models as lex/coherent functors on a syntactic category); reconstruction of a structure from Def(M)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Makkai–Reyes, 'First order categorical logic' (1977); later categorical model theory

ideas.what: Tame maps as morphisms of Esp_mod, with images and inverse images of tame parts tame
ideas.modern_name: Definable maps; stability of definable sets under images and preimages

ideas.what: Inductive limits / gluings of tame spaces (finite unions, pushouts, criterion that a tame structure on the set-colimit making the maps tame gives the categorical colimit)
ideas.modern_name: Definable spaces by gluing; colimits in categories of definable spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries 1998, ch. 10; Robson; Delfs–Knebusch (semialgebraic/locally semialgebraic spaces, 1980s)

missed.claim: Grothendieck recasts his axiomatic tame structure (an o-minimal-type structure) categorically as a finitely complete category with a left exact fibre functor to Sets and a generating object R. This is essentially the 'category of definable sets' viewpoint of categorical logic, applied to tame topology at a date (1973-78 per the archive) before o-minimality was formalized. The tame-topology/o-minimality literature does not usually present structures this way or credit such a reconstruction to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: On trouve que la donnée d'un M_* est équivalente à la donnée du système (à isom. près) (E, R, X ↦ |X|) a) la catégorie E avec lim finies b) le foncteur X ↦ |X| E → (Ens), exact à gauche c) l'objet R ∈ Ob E tel que tout objet [de E] se plonge dans un R^n.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a functorial, 'Tannakian-style' entry point to o-minimal geometry: a structure as a pair (category, fibre functor) plus a generator. This links to current categorical and condensed/stacky approaches to tame and definable geometry (e.g. definable sheaves, o-minimal sheaf theory, Bakker–Brunebarbe–Tsimerman definable analytic spaces). It is also historically relevant to Grothendieck's priority in tame topology.

missed.claim: Section III on inductive limits and gluing of tame spaces is only begun. The question of which colimits exist in Esp_mod and are preserved by |.| is posed, followed by a partial criterion on the next page.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Colimits of definable spaces (quotients, gluing along non-closed subsets) remain delicate, e.g. definable quotients and elimination of imaginaries. Grothendieck's framing via the lex functor |.| could be compared with existing results, but it is not developed here.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sketches an axiomatic o-minimal-type framework predating the standard theory, and states a neat categorical reconstruction (structure <-> lex category + fibre functor + generating object). That reconstruction is conceptually close to known categorical logic and is stated without the needed faithfulness/image conditions. It is a notable unpublished detail of historical interest rather than a new theorem.
transcription_corrections: 'On s'imagine' should most likely read 'On récupère'. The inserted line '{+aisément les R^n correspondants+}' is likely 'récupère ... les R^n correspondants', meaning one recovers M_n as the set of subobjects of R^n.
In c), 'tout objet de R se plonge' should read 'tout objet de E se plonge dans un R^n'.
The insertion '(produits dans E)' refers to R^n being the product taken in E.
Left margin: roughly 'Introduire les fonctions modérées comme morphismes de Esp_M, ... sous-objets ..., les propriétés de f(A), f^{-1}(B)'.
The interlinear insertion before (III) reads approximately 'Parler aussi des applications modérées d'esp. modérés dans des R^I, d'où produits cartésiens'.
'jonction(s)' in Section III may be 'réunions' or 'recollements' (gluings); uncertain.
